place.en: Dwarkanath Memorial Library · the rare book room · Saturday, 10:30 AM

brief.en: Nine volumes have come back to the shelf this year lighter by exactly one engraving each, and not one of them looks touched. Where the plate was there is a plate: same image, same foxing, same brown edge. It is simply not the one that was bound in eighteen forty-nine, and four of the real ones are in a dealer’s fair catalogue with the library’s shelf-mark still ghosting through the margin.

photoCaption.en: the hooker frontispiece, under raking light

iraNote.en: “A copperplate bruises the paper. A press only puts ink on it. Feel the back of the sheet before you look at the front.”

teaser.en: Rare books return to the shelf lighter by exactly one engraving, and the substitute is good enough to sit there for a year.

text.en: The plate mark is printed, not embossed. A copper plate under a rolling press bruises the sheet; this one is flat as a wall.
No chain lines, no watermark, and it lights up under ultraviolet. Machine paper, aged in tea and pressed dry.
Section four of every one of the nine is re-sewn in linen of a different twist to the rest of its own book.
Nine volumes out to the binder and back. Nine volumes short a plate. The lists are the same list.
Four hand-coloured plates, “removed from a broken copy”. On lot 12 the library’s own shelf-mark still ghosts through the margin.
Each of the nine was last called for by a reader in the weeks before it went out for repair. Six different readers.
₹22 outstanding since April on a reference loan.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — a scholar who owes twenty-two rupees is every scholar who has ever used this room

text.en: A damp patch behind the folio shelf, freshly limewashed.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — the damp took the almanacs on the bottom shelf, and no almanac is missing a plate

text.en: A rare-room key reported lost in February and the lock changed in March.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — the lock was changed before six of the nine ever went out

text.en: Evenings at a press on Bidhan Sarani, on the folding table.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — half the men in this lane fold sheets in the evenings; folding is not engraving

text.en: The Roxburgh volume’s front hinge, split along the joint.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — that hinge has been split since the 1978 flood and the register says so

text.en: “I chose all nine off the shelf myself and sent them out on my own signature. They went to one binder, because there is one binder in this city I trust.”
“I buy plates out of broken copies. Everyone in this trade does. He brings them in a folder, four or five at a time, and I have never once asked which copy they broke.”

hook.en: the only hands that opened all nine

confession.en: Cut one plate from each of the nine while they were unsewn on his bench, laid in a photographic facsimile on tea-aged machine paper, and re-sewed section four in his own linen.

hook.en: sent every one of the nine out for repair

alibi.en: She picked the nine off the shelf herself and signed for each, which is a complete written record of her own involvement. Nobody documents a theft nine times in their own hand.

hook.en: four of the plates are in his catalogue

alibi.en: He printed the shelf-mark, the provenance and his own name in a catalogue circulated to two thousand collectors. That is not concealment; that is a man who never thought to look.

hook.en: her slips are on five of the nine

alibi.en: She called for five of them, and she is the reason anybody knows: she wrote to the trustees in June saying a plate looked wrong. Her slips are on the volumes because she is the only person reading them.

hook.en: carries every volume to and from the binder

alibi.en: He carries them tied in a cloth and hands them over sealed, and the seals came back unbroken every time. The books were opened at the far end of the journey, not on it.

setting.en: The reading room, ledgers open in front of her, spectacles pushed up.

ask.en: How does a book leave this room?

answer.en: “On my signature, in a cloth, sealed, with the peon. It has not changed since the trust was founded.”

note.en: Sealed both ways. So the opening happened where the opening is supposed to happen.

ask.en: Miss Sen wrote to the trustees in June.

answer.en: “She did, and I sent for the volume the same afternoon, and I could not see what she meant. Neither could the trustees.”

note.en: A facsimile good enough to survive being looked for. That is a professional’s work, not a reader’s.

ask.en: All nine went to the same man.

answer.en: “I chose all nine off the shelf myself and sent them out on my own signature. They went to one binder, because there is one binder in this city I trust.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the repair register. Two lists that turn out to be one list is a thing to lay in front of her, not to describe.

note.en: Nine books, one bench. The list of the damaged and the list of the robbed are the same nine names.

setting.en: The shop on Free School Street, plates in mylar sleeves under the glass.

ask.en: Where do loose plates come from?

answer.en: “Broken copies. Damp, white ants, a family selling a grandfather’s shelf. There is nothing rarer in this trade than a whole book.”

note.en: True, and it is exactly the sentence that makes this possible.

ask.en: Lot 12 carries this library’s shelf-mark in the margin.

answer.en: “I buy plates out of broken copies. He brings them in a folder, four or five at a time, and I have never once asked which copy they broke.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the fair catalogue. He will not discuss a margin he has not been shown in print.

note.en: He printed the shelf-mark himself, in two thousand catalogues, and never read it.

answer.en: “A binder. In this city there are perhaps four who could, and only one of them works for a library.”

note.en: Four men who could. One of them with nine sealed cloth bundles a year.

setting.en: The bindery off Baithakkhana Road, a book in the press, linen thread on a spool.

answer.en: “The book, opened. You cannot mend a spine with the sections in. Everything comes apart before anything gets better.”

note.en: Everything comes apart. He said it with some love, which makes it worse.

ask.en: The substitute leaves are machine paper.

answer.en: “Then somebody has done poor work. I would have used a flyleaf out of a dead book — there is no shortage of them.”

note.en: He is critiquing the forgery. A man who has never seen it would ask what it looked like.

ask.en: Section four of all nine is re-sewn in the same linen, and it is not the linen the books were bound in.

answer.en: He looks at the spool on the bench for a while. “That is my thread. There is one spool and it is mine.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the sewing slip. He knows more about thread than anyone in Bengal; do not go in without it.

note.en: Nine books, one section each, one spool. He did not even change the twist.

correction.en: Twenty-two rupees of overdue fine is not a reason. Four hand-coloured plates in a fair catalogue, priced, is.
A lost key that was changed in March cannot open six books that left in April. Nine volumes, unsewn on one bench, by one pair of hands — that is the opening.
A split hinge from the 1978 flood hides nothing. A facsimile on tea-aged machine paper, sewn back in and shelved, is what bought this a whole year.

text.en: That frontispiece was printed, not engraved. So somebody had the book open — and this library keeps a list of every volume that has been opened.
